title: Explore Relationships Between Two Variables
contentObjective: I can recognize when two quantities change together, and identify which one is the independent variable and which is the dependent variable.
languageObjective: I can explain which quantity depends on the other using the words independent variable, dependent variable, and depends on.

noticeStarters: I notice the tallest plants are ___ .
I notice all three trays got ___ .
wonderStarters: I wonder why the two quantities ___ .

vocabulary.definition: The quantity that is subject to choice. It does not depend on the other quantity.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad que se elige. No depende de la otra cantidad.
vocabulary.example: The hours of sunlight a tray receives — Akela chooses that.
vocabulary.visual: Miguel picks the number of MONTHS — nothing else decides it for him.
vocabulary.cloze: The quantity that is subject to choice is the ___ ___.

examples.text: The number of tickets you decide to buy
examples.why: You choose it; nothing in the problem forces the value.

examples.text: The total cost of those tickets
examples.why: The cost is the result of your choice, so it depends.

vocabulary.definition: The quantity that changes in response to the independent variable.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad que cambia en respuesta a la variable independiente.
vocabulary.example: The height the plants reach — it responds to the sunlight.
vocabulary.visual: Total cost = $24.95 × months — the cost RESPONDS to the months.
vocabulary.cloze: The quantity that changes in response to the other is the ___ ___.

examples.text: Calories burned during a jog of the length you chose
examples.why: It moves because the minutes moved.

examples.text: The minutes you decided to jog
examples.why: That is the choice, not the response.

vocabulary.definition: One quantity depends on another when changing the first causes the second to change.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cantidad depende de otra cuando cambiar la primera hace cambiar la segunda.
vocabulary.visual: “Total cost depends on the number of months.” Responder first, chooser last.
vocabulary.cloze: Say it in order: the responding quantity ___ ___ the chosen one.

examples.text: Pages printed depends on minutes running
examples.why: The printer's output responds to the time you let it run.

examples.text: Minutes running depends on pages printed
examples.why: It reverses the roles — you set the time, not the pages.

vocabulary.definition: Something that can be counted or measured.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Algo que se puede contar o medir.
vocabulary.example: Hours of sunlight, centimeters of height, minutes of jogging.
vocabulary.visual: 24.95 dollars per month, 12 months — each is a number with a meaning.
vocabulary.cloze: Something that can be counted or measured is a ___.

examples.why: A number together with what it measures.
A name cannot be counted or measured.

vocabulary.example: More sunlight goes with taller plants.
vocabulary.visual: 1 month → $24.95, 2 months → $49.90: the two quantities move together.

turnAndTalk.question: Akela put her three bean trays in three different spots, so each got a different amount of sunlight. After three weeks she measured the height of the plants. Which of those two quantities did Akela choose, and which one responded?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Akela chose where to place each tray, which set the hours of sunlight; the plant height was measured afterward, in response to the sunlight.

stems.en: Akela chose ___, so ___ is the independent variable.
stems.es: Akela eligió ___, así que ___ es la variable independiente.

stems.en: Plant height is the dependent variable because it ___.
stems.es: La altura de la planta es la variable dependiente porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer names sunlight as chosen (independent) and height as responding (dependent), and can say the sentence 'height depends on sunlight.' A weak answer just says 'height is bigger' without naming which quantity was chosen.
turnAndTalk.extend: Claire chose to jog for 30 minutes and burned 123 Calories. Later she chose to run exactly 3 miles and recorded how long it took. Explain why time is independent in one problem but dependent in the other.
extendStems: In the jogging problem, ___ is independent because Claire chose it, but in the distance problem, ___ is independent instead.
The same quantity can switch roles because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: When you sorted the eight cards into independent and dependent, how did you decide where 'number of Calories Claire burns' belonged?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Calories burned is subject to choice — no, it responds to how long Claire jogs, which makes it the dependent variable.

stems.en: I put ___ in the dependent column because it ___.
stems.es: Puse ___ en la columna dependiente porque ___.

stems.en: ___ belongs with independent because someone gets to ___ it.
stems.es: ___ pertenece con independiente porque alguien puede ___ eso.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for the test 'who gets to choose this' rather than which number is bigger or which was mentioned first in the problem. A weak answer just repeats the card's category without justifying it.
turnAndTalk.extend: The card 'number of months you keep a gym membership' and 'total amount you have paid the gym' were also sorted. Justify why 'total amount paid' can never be the independent variable in this pair.
extendStems: Total amount paid can't be independent because ___.
It always responds to ___, which is the quantity a person actually decides.

turnAndTalk.question: At the pizza shop, the number of employees (6) and the topping limit (3) stay fixed no matter how many pizzas are made, but the cost of cheese changes with every pizza. Why do employees and toppings NOT count as part of a dependent relationship here?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A dependent relationship needs a quantity that actually changes in response to another; a fixed number like 6 employees never changes, so it can't depend on anything.

stems.en: The number of employees is fixed at ___, so it doesn't ___ when pizzas change.
stems.es: El número de empleados es fijo en ___, así que no ___ cuando cambian las pizzas.

stems.en: Cost of cheese depends on pizzas because each pizza adds $___.
stems.es: El costo del queso depende de las pizzas porque cada pizza agrega $___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer explains that dependence requires movement — a constant like 6 employees can't be 'dependent' on anything because it never changes. A weak answer just says 'employees isn't a variable' without explaining why.
turnAndTalk.extend: If the shop made 20 pizzas instead of a smaller batch, would the number of employees ever become 7? Use that answer to explain the difference between a variable and a fixed quantity.
extendStems: No, because the number of employees ___ no matter how many pizzas are made.
A variable can ___, but a fixed quantity stays ___.

turnAndTalk.question: Look back at a practice problem where you had to name the independent and dependent variable. What question did you ask yourself first?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The test for independent is 'who or what gets to choose this quantity' — the other quantity is dependent because it responds.

stems.en: First I asked myself ___, which told me ___ was independent.
stems.es: Primero me pregunté ___, lo cual me dijo que ___ era independiente.

stems.en: I knew ___ was dependent because it ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for a repeatable strategy ("ask what's chosen") rather than a guess based on which number looked bigger or came first in the sentence.
turnAndTalk.extend: A classmate said 'minutes jogged depends on Calories burned' and got it backward. How would you help them fix their thinking using one vocabulary word?
extendStems: I'd tell them to check which quantity is ___ first — that one goes second in the sentence.
The mistake happens when you name the ___ variable as if it were the ___ variable.

launch.narrative: Akela planted three trays of bean seeds for a science experiment. Each tray sat in a different spot, so each got a different amount of sunlight per day. After three weeks she measured the average plant height in every tray. Two quantities in that experiment are related: change the sunlight and the height changes with it. One of them Akela chose, and the other one answered back. Today you will name which quantity is the independent one and which depends on it, and you will find pairs like this in a jogging tracker and a pizza shop.

conceptIntro.heading: Which quantity is doing the changing — and which is responding?
conceptIntro.intro: When two quantities are related, one of them depends on the other. Naming which is which is the whole job of this lesson.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Independent & Dependent Variables. 1. Independent Variable (x): The input / cause that is chosen or changes freely. 2. Dependent Variable (y): The output / effect that depends on the independent variable. 3. Sentence check: 'The (dependent) depends on the (independent)'

iDo.title: Watch me sort Akela's experiment
lines: The two quantities are hours of sunlight per day and average plant height after 3 weeks.
Akela CHOSE where to put each tray, so she chose the sunlight. Sunlight is subject to choice — that makes it the independent variable.
She did not choose how tall the plants got. Height responded. That makes height the dependent variable.
Say it as a sentence: plant height depends on sunlight.
linesEs: Las dos cantidades son las horas de luz solar al día y la altura promedio de la planta después de 3 semanas.
Akela eligió dónde poner cada charola, así que eligió la luz solar. La luz solar está sujeta a elección — eso la hace la variable independiente.
Ella no eligió qué tan altas crecieron las plantas. La altura respondió. Eso hace que la altura sea la variable dependiente.
Dilo como una oración: la altura de la planta depende de la luz solar.
iDo.titleEs: Mírame clasificar el experimento de Akela

weDo.title: Let's try Claire's fitness tracker together
lines: Claire burned 123 Calories on a 30-minute jog and 246 Calories on a 60-minute jog.
Which did Claire choose — the minutes, or the Calories?
She chose how long to jog. So time is independent, and Calories burned is dependent.
linesEs: Claire quemó 123 calorías en una carrera de 30 minutos y 246 calorías en una de 60 minutos.
¿Qué eligió Claire — los minutos o las calorías?
Ella eligió cuánto tiempo correr. Así que el tiempo es independiente, y las calorías quemadas son dependientes.

Then finish the sentence: ___ depends on ___ .

conceptIntro.headingEs: ¿Qué cantidad es la que cambia — y cuál responde?
conceptIntro.introEs: Cuando dos cantidades están relacionadas, una de ellas depende de la otra. Nombrar cuál es cuál es todo el trabajo de esta lección.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Variables independientes y dependientes. 1. Variable independiente (x): la entrada o causa que se elige o cambia libremente. 2. Variable dependiente (y): la salida o efecto que depende de la variable independiente. 3. Comprobación con una oración: «(la dependiente) depende de (la independiente)»

discourse.prompt: Take a card you and your partner put in different columns. Say the sentence 'The ___ depends on the ___' out loud both ways — which version is true, and how does that settle which variable is independent?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The ___ depends on the ___, so ___ is the independent variable.

discourse.sentenceFrameEs: El ___ depende del ___, así que ___ es la variable independiente.

connect.scenario: At a local pizza shop a customer can order up to three toppings on a large pizza. The shop has 6 employees. The shop spends $1.15 on cheese and $1.95 on sauce for each pizza it makes.
connect.promptQuestion: Which two quantities in this shop are related, so that one depends on the other — and which quantity does NOT depend on the number of pizzas at all?
connect.prompt: In this scenario, the ___ is the independent variable. The ___ and the ___ both depend on it. The number of ___ stays the same no matter how many pizzas are made.

check.stem: The number of pizzas made each week determines other costs at the shop. Which variable is the independent variable in this relationship?
check.explanation: The number of pizzas is independent because it is the value that determines the other costs. Cost of cheese is dependent because it changes as a result of pizzas made; the number of employees and toppings allowed are fixed limits, not quantities that change with pizza count.
check.stemEs: El número de pizzas que se hacen cada semana determina otros costos de la pizzería. ¿Qué variable es la variable independiente en esta relación?
check.explanationEs: El número de pizzas es independiente porque es el valor que determina los demás costos. El costo del queso es dependiente porque cambia como resultado de las pizzas que se hacen; el número de empleados y los ingredientes permitidos son límites fijos, no cantidades que cambian con el número de pizzas.

check.stem: Which two quantities have a dependent relationship in this scenario?
choices: cost of cheese and number of pizzas made
number of employees and number of pizzas made
number of toppings allowed and cost of sauce
number of employees and number of toppings allowed
check.explanation: The cost of cheese rises as more pizzas are made ($1.15 per pizza), so it depends on the number of pizzas. The number of employees (6) and the topping limit (3) are fixed values that stay the same no matter how many pizzas are made, so they are not part of a dependent relationship here.
check.stemEs: ¿Qué dos cantidades tienen una relación dependiente en esta situación?
check.explanationEs: El costo del queso sube conforme se hacen más pizzas ($1.15 por pizza), así que depende del número de pizzas. El número de empleados (6) y el límite de ingredientes (3) son valores fijos que se quedan igual sin importar cuántas pizzas se hagan, así que no son parte de una relación dependiente aquí.
choicesEs: costo del queso y número de pizzas hechas
número de empleados y número de pizzas hechas
número de ingredientes permitidos y costo de la salsa
número de empleados y número de ingredientes permitidos

check.stem: The shop makes 20 pizzas in a week. Which of these does NOT depend on the number of pizzas sold?
choices: the total spent on cheese and sauce combined
check.explanation: Staff count (6 employees) is fixed and stays the same regardless of pizza volume. Cheese cost, sauce cost, and their combined total all scale up as more pizzas are made, so those three DO depend on the number of pizzas.
check.stemEs: La pizzería hace 20 pizzas en una semana. ¿Cuál de estas no depende del número de pizzas vendidas?
check.explanationEs: El número de personal (6 empleados) es fijo y se queda igual sin importar el volumen de pizzas. El costo del queso, el de la salsa y su total combinado suben conforme se hacen más pizzas, así que esos tres sí dependen del número de pizzas.
choicesEs: el costo total de la salsa
el total gastado en queso y salsa juntos

connect.modelAnswer: The cost of cheese each week depends on the number of pizzas the shop makes, so the number of pizzas is the independent variable and the cheese cost is the dependent variable. The number of employees is 6 no matter how many pizzas are sold, so it does not depend on the number of pizzas.
connect.promptEs: En esta situación, ___ es la variable independiente. ___ y ___ dependen de ella. El número de ___ se queda igual sin importar cuántas pizzas se hagan.
connect.scenarioEs: En una pizzería local un cliente puede pedir hasta tres ingredientes en una pizza grande. La pizzería tiene 6 empleados. La pizzería gasta $1.15 en queso y $1.95 en salsa por cada pizza que hace.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿Qué dos cantidades de esta pizzería están relacionadas, de modo que una depende de la otra — y qué cantidad no depende para nada del número de pizzas?
connect.modelAnswerEs: El costo del queso cada semana depende del número de pizzas que hace la pizzería, así que el número de pizzas es la variable independiente y el costo del queso es la variable dependiente. El número de empleados es 6 sin importar cuántas pizzas se vendan, así que no depende del número de pizzas.

exitTicket.stem: A dog walker charges by the hour. Which sentence is correct?
choices: The total charge depends on the number of hours, so hours is the independent variable.
The number of hours depends on the total charge, so the charge is the independent variable.
Neither quantity depends on the other.
exitTicket.explanation: The walker chooses how many hours to work; the money that results responds to that choice. Hours is subject to choice, so hours is independent and the total charge is dependent.
hints: Which one does someone get to CHOOSE?
Say it out loud: '___ depends on ___ .' Which order sounds true?
The quantity that responds is the dependent one.
exitTicket.stemEs: Un paseador de perros cobra por hora. ¿Qué oración es correcta?
choicesEs: El cargo total depende del número de horas, así que las horas son la variable independiente.
El número de horas depende del cargo total, así que el cargo es la variable independiente.
Las dos cantidades son variables independientes.
Ninguna cantidad depende de la otra.
exitTicket.explanationEs: El paseador escoge cuántas horas trabajar; el dinero que resulta responde a esa elección. Las horas se pueden escoger, así que las horas son independientes y el cargo total es dependiente.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál de las dos puede escoger alguien?
Dilo en voz alta: «___ depende de ___ .» ¿Qué orden suena verdadero?
La cantidad que responde es la dependiente.

approaching.stem: Akela chooses how many hours of sunlight each tray gets. Which is the INDEPENDENT variable?
approaching.explanation: Akela chooses the sunlight, so sunlight is subject to choice — that makes it independent.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
The number of trays is not one of the two quantities being related here.
The number of seeds is not one of the two quantities being related here.
hints: Which quantity did Akela get to decide?
Sunlight was set by where she put the tray.
The one subject to choice is independent.
approaching.stemEs: Akela escoge cuántas horas de luz solar recibe cada bandeja. ¿Cuál es la variable INDEPENDIENTE?
approaching.explanationEs: Akela escoge la luz solar, así que la luz solar es lo que se escoge — eso la hace independiente.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál cantidad pudo decidir Akela?
La luz solar la determinó dónde puso la bandeja.
La que se escoge es la independiente.

approaching.stem: In Akela's experiment, which is the DEPENDENT variable?
approaching.explanation: Height responds to how much sunlight the tray received, so height is the dependent variable.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
The kind of seed was the same for all three trays.
The tray size was the same for all three trays.
hints: Which quantity RESPONDED to the other?
Akela did not choose how tall the plants grew.
The responding quantity is dependent.
approaching.stemEs: En el experimento de Akela, ¿cuál es la variable DEPENDIENTE?
approaching.explanationEs: La altura responde a cuánta luz solar recibió la bandeja, así que la altura es la variable dependiente.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál cantidad RESPONDIÓ a la otra?
Akela no escogió qué tan alto crecieron las plantas.
La cantidad que responde es la dependiente.

approaching.stem: Claire burned 123 Calories on a 30-minute jog. Which quantity is subject to choice?
approaching.explanation: Claire decides how long to jog. The Calories follow from that decision.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
Heart rate is not one of the two quantities in this problem.
The weather is not one of the two quantities in this problem.
hints: What does Claire decide before she starts?
She sets the time on the tracker.
Calories are the result, not the choice.
approaching.stemEs: Claire quemó 123 calorías en un trote de 30 minutos. ¿Cuál cantidad es la que se escoge?
approaching.explanationEs: Claire decide cuánto tiempo trotar. Las calorías dependen de esa decisión.
hintsEs: ¿Qué decide Claire antes de empezar?
Ella fija el tiempo en el reloj.
Las calorías son el resultado, no la decisión.

approaching.stem: Which sentence is written in the correct order?
choices: Calories burned depends on minutes jogged.
Minutes jogged depends on Calories burned.
Calories burned depends on Calories burned.
Neither quantity depends on the other.
approaching.explanation: The dependent quantity comes first in the sentence '___ depends on ___ .' Calories respond to time, so Calories depend on minutes.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
A quantity cannot depend on itself.
These two quantities are clearly related — more time means more Calories.
hints: Say both versions out loud. Which one is true?
Claire chooses the minutes.
The responder goes first: 'responder depends on chooser.'
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál oración está escrita en el orden correcto?
approaching.explanationEs: La cantidad dependiente va primero en la oración '___ depende de ___ .' Las calorías responden al tiempo, así que las calorías dependen de los minutos.
hintsEs: Di en voz alta las dos versiones. ¿Cuál es verdadera?
Claire escoge los minutos.
El que responde va primero: 'el que responde depende del que escoge'.

approaching.stem: A tray that got 2 hours of sun grew to 4 cm. A tray that got 6 hours grew to 12 cm. As sunlight increases, plant height…
approaching.explanation: 2 hours gave 4 cm and 6 hours gave 12 cm, so more sunlight went with more height.
choiceFeedback: Look again: the taller plants got MORE sun, not less.
The heights are different (4 cm and 12 cm), so it did not stay the same.
Both data points are given, so you can compare them.
hints: Compare the two trays.
2 hours to 6 hours is an increase. 4 cm to 12 cm is what?
Both went up together.
approaching.stemEs: Una bandeja que recibió 2 horas de sol creció a 4 cm. Una bandeja que recibió 6 horas creció a 12 cm. Conforme aumenta la luz solar, la altura de la planta…
approaching.explanationEs: 2 horas dieron 4 cm y 6 horas dieron 12 cm, así que más luz solar vino con más altura.
hintsEs: Compara las dos bandejas.
De 2 horas a 6 horas hay un aumento. De 4 cm a 12 cm, ¿qué hay?
Los dos subieron juntos.

approaching.stem: You buy tickets at $45 each. Which quantity depends on the other?
choices: Total cost depends on number of tickets
Number of tickets depends on total cost
The price per ticket depends on the total cost
approaching.explanation: You choose how many tickets to buy; the total cost is the result of that choice.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
The price is fixed at $45 — it does not respond to the total.
Buying more tickets clearly changes the total, so they are related.
hints: Which number do you pick at the counter?
You choose a count of tickets.
The total is what comes back to you.
approaching.stemEs: Compras boletos a $45 cada uno. ¿Cuál cantidad depende de la otra?
approaching.explanationEs: Tú escoges cuántos boletos comprar; el costo total es el resultado de esa decisión.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál número escoges en el mostrador?
Tú escoges una cantidad de boletos.
El total es lo que regresa a ti.

approaching.instructions: Sort each quantity: is it the independent variable (the input you choose) or the dependent variable (the output that responds)?
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada cantidad: ¿es la variable independiente (la entrada que eliges) o la variable dependiente (la salida que responde)?
approaching.label: Sort each quantity: independent or dependent?

categories.label: Independent variable (input)
items: Hours of sunlight a tray of seedlings gets
itemsEs: Horas de luz solar que recibe una bandeja de plántulas

hints: Use the sentence check: 'The ___ depends on the ___.' The first blank is dependent.
The independent variable is the one a person chooses or controls directly.
hintsEs: Usa la oración de comprobación: 'El/La ___ depende de el/la ___.' El primer espacio es la dependiente.
La variable independiente es la que una persona elige o controla directamente.
approaching.explanation: Each pair passes the sentence check: the height depends on the sunlight, the cost depends on the months, and the Calories depend on the minutes. The chosen quantity — sunlight, months, minutes — is independent; the quantity that responds is dependent.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada par pasa la oración de comprobación: la altura depende de la luz solar, el costo depende de los meses y las calorías dependen de los minutos. La cantidad elegida — luz, meses, minutos — es independiente; la que responde es dependiente.

onLevel.stem: A gym charges $24.95 per month. Which pair correctly names the variables?
onLevel.explanation: You choose how many months to stay a member. The total cost responds to that.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
$24.95 is a fixed rate, not a variable that changes.
$24.95 is a fixed rate, not the responding quantity.
hints: Which number can the member change?
Months is the choice.
Cost responds to months.
onLevel.stemEs: Un gimnasio cobra $24.95 al mes. ¿Cuál par nombra correctamente las variables?
onLevel.explanationEs: Tú escoges cuántos meses seguir siendo miembro. El costo total responde a eso.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál número puede cambiar el miembro?
Los meses son lo que se escoge.
El costo responde a los meses.

onLevel.stem: Claire jogs 30 minutes and burns 123 Calories. At the same rate, how many Calories would a 90-minute jog burn?
onLevel.explanation: 30 minutes burned 123 Calories, and 90 is 3 times 30, so the Calories are 3 times 123, which is 369.
choiceFeedback: 246 Calories is the 60-minute jog, not the 90-minute jog.
That is not the result of tripling 123.
That is a rounded guess — scale 123 by the same factor as the time.
hints: How many times longer is 90 minutes than 30 minutes?
90 divided by 30 is 3.
Multiply 123 by 3.
onLevel.stemEs: Claire trota 30 minutos y quema 123 calorías. A la misma tasa, ¿cuántas calorías quemaría un trote de 90 minutos?
onLevel.explanationEs: 30 minutos quemaron 123 calorías, y 90 es 3 veces 30, así que las calorías son 3 veces 123, o sea 369.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas veces más largo es 90 minutos que 30 minutos?
90 dividido entre 30 es 3.
Multiplica 123 por 3.

onLevel.stem: Which of these pairs is NOT a dependent relationship?
choices: Number of pizzas sold and number of employees the shop has
Number of pizzas sold and weekly cost of cheese
onLevel.explanation: The shop has 6 employees whether it sells 5 pizzas or 500. That count does not respond to pizza sales.
choiceFeedback: Cheese cost DOES rise with more pizzas, so this pair is related.
Calories DO rise with more jogging, so this pair is related.
Cost DOES rise with more tickets, so this pair is related.
hints: Which one stays the same no matter what?
The staff list does not change when a pizza is sold.
Look for the pair that does not move together.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cuál de estos pares NO es una relación de dependencia?
onLevel.explanationEs: La tienda tiene 6 empleados ya sea que venda 5 pizzas o 500. Esa cantidad no responde a las ventas de pizza.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál se mantiene igual pase lo que pase?
La lista de empleados no cambia cuando se vende una pizza.
Busca el par que no cambia junto.

onLevel.stem: A plant grows 2 cm for every hour of daily sunlight. Which table row is correct?
onLevel.explanation: At 2 cm per hour, 4 hours of sunlight gives 4 times 2, which is 8 cm.
choiceFeedback: That adds 2 instead of multiplying by 2.
That is the growth for a single hour, not for 4 hours.
That copies the number of hours instead of multiplying by the 2 cm rate.
hints: What does each hour add?
Each hour adds 2 cm.
4 hours means 4 groups of 2 cm.
onLevel.stemEs: Una planta crece 2 cm por cada hora de luz solar al día. ¿Cuál fila de la tabla es correcta?
onLevel.explanationEs: A 2 cm por hora, 4 horas de luz solar dan 4 por 2, que son 8 cm.
hintsEs: ¿Cuánto suma cada hora?
Cada hora suma 2 cm.
4 horas significan 4 grupos de 2 cm.

onLevel.stem: Which question would you ask to find the DEPENDENT variable?
choices: Which quantity responds when the other one changes?
onLevel.explanation: The dependent variable is defined by its response to the independent variable — not by size, units, or name.
choiceFeedback: Size has nothing to do with which variable is dependent.
Both quantities usually have units.
Alphabetical order has nothing to do with mathematics here.
hints: Go back to the definition.
Dependent means it changes in response.
Ask what responds.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cuál pregunta harías para hallar la variable DEPENDIENTE?
onLevel.explanationEs: La variable dependiente se define por cómo responde a la variable independiente — no por su tamaño, sus unidades ni su nombre.
hintsEs: Vuelve a la definición.
Dependiente significa que cambia en respuesta.
Pregunta qué responde.

onLevel.stem: Claire decides to walk instead of jog for the same 30 minutes. What happens to the two variables?
choices: Time stays the independent variable; Calories burned still depends on it
Calories burned becomes the independent variable
Neither is a variable any more
onLevel.explanation: Changing the activity changes how many Calories each minute burns, but time is still the quantity she chooses.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
Both quantities still change and are still related.
You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
hints: Does Claire still choose the minutes?
Yes — she sets the time either way.
The roles do not swap when the rate changes.
onLevel.stemEs: Claire decide caminar en vez de trotar durante los mismos 30 minutos. ¿Qué pasa con las dos variables?
onLevel.explanationEs: Cambiar la actividad cambia cuántas calorías quema cada minuto, pero el tiempo sigue siendo la cantidad que ella escoge.
hintsEs: ¿Claire sigue escogiendo los minutos?
Sí — ella fija el tiempo en ambos casos.
Los papeles no se intercambian cuando cambia la tasa.

onLevel.stem: If Claire runs exactly 3 miles and records how long it takes, which is the independent variable now?
onLevel.explanation: This time she fixes the distance by choice and the time is whatever results, so distance is independent and time is dependent.
choiceFeedback: Time is now the result, not the choice — the roles have flipped from the earlier problem.
Speed is not one of the two quantities she set or recorded.
Calories are not mentioned in this version of the problem.
hints: What did Claire decide in advance this time?
She decided the distance: 3 miles.
Whatever she measures afterward is the dependent one.
onLevel.stemEs: Si Claire corre exactamente 3 millas y registra cuánto tiempo tarda, ¿cuál es ahora la variable independiente?
onLevel.explanationEs: Esta vez ella fija la distancia por decisión y el tiempo es lo que resulte, así que la distancia es independiente y el tiempo es dependiente.
hintsEs: ¿Qué decidió Claire de antemano esta vez?
Ella decidió la distancia: 3 millas.
Lo que ella mida después es la dependiente.

onLevel.label: Claire burns Calories at a steady rate: 30 minutes burns 123 Calories. Complete the table.
onLevel.labelEs: Claire quema calorías a un ritmo constante: 30 minutos queman 123 calorías. Completa la tabla.
hints: 60 minutes is twice 30 minutes, so it burns twice the Calories.
The Calories column DEPENDS on the minutes column — that is what makes it the dependent variable.
hintsEs: 60 minutos es el doble de 30 minutos, así que quema el doble de calorías.
La columna de calorías DEPENDE de la columna de minutos: eso la hace la variable dependiente.
onLevel.explanation: Because the rate is steady, doubling the minutes doubles the Calories: 60 minutes burns 246, and 90 minutes burns 369. The table shows dependence in action — every value in the Calories column is produced by a value in the minutes column.
onLevel.explanationEs: Como el ritmo es constante, duplicar los minutos duplica las calorías: 60 minutos queman 246 y 90 minutos queman 369. La tabla muestra la dependencia en acción: cada valor de la columna de calorías es producido por un valor de la columna de minutos.

extending.stem: Two quantities are related. Which statement is ALWAYS true?
choices: The independent variable is subject to choice
The independent variable is always the larger number
The dependent variable is always measured in dollars
The independent variable is always listed first in a table
extending.explanation: Being subject to choice is the definition. Size, units, and table position are not part of it.
choiceFeedback: A choice can be a small number — 1 hour is independent just as much as 100 hours.
Dependent variables can be centimeters, Calories, miles — anything that responds.
Table layout is a convention, not a definition.
hints: Which option restates the definition?
Definitions do not depend on size or units.
Choice is the deciding test.
extending.stemEs: Dos cantidades están relacionadas. ¿Cuál enunciado es SIEMPRE verdadero?
extending.explanationEs: Ser lo que uno escoge es la definición. El tamaño, las unidades y la posición en la tabla no forman parte de ella.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál opción repite la definición?
Las definiciones no dependen del tamaño ni de las unidades.
Lo que se escoge es la prueba decisiva.

extending.stem: Give an example where the SAME quantity can be independent in one problem and dependent in another.
choices: Time: chosen when you pick how long to jog, but measured as a result when you run a set distance
A quantity can never switch roles
extending.explanation: Claire's two problems show exactly this: minutes is a choice in one and a result in the other.
choiceFeedback: Compare Claire's two jogs — in the 3-mile version time is the result.
In the 30-minute jog Claire chose the time, so it was independent there.
The role depends on the problem, not on the quantity itself.
hints: Look back at Claire's two problems.
In one she set minutes; in the other she set miles.
The role depends on what was chosen.
extending.stemEs: Da un ejemplo donde la MISMA cantidad pueda ser independiente en un problema y dependiente en otro.
extending.explanationEs: Los dos problemas de Claire muestran exactamente esto: los minutos son una decisión en uno y un resultado en el otro.
hintsEs: Vuelve a mirar los dos problemas de Claire.
En uno ella fijó los minutos; en el otro fijó las millas.
El papel depende de lo que se escogió.

extending.stem: The pizza shop spends $1.15 on cheese per pizza. Which weekly total is correct if it makes 200 pizzas?
extending.explanation: 200 pizzas at $1.15 each is 200 times 1.15, which is $230.
choiceFeedback: That is the cost for 100 pizzas, not 200.
That adds the numbers instead of multiplying them.
That multiplies as if each pizza cost $5.75.
hints: What operation joins a per-pizza cost and a count?
Multiply the rate by the number of pizzas.
extending.stemEs: La pizzería gasta $1.15 en queso por pizza. ¿Cuál total semanal es correcto si hace 200 pizzas?
extending.explanationEs: 200 pizzas a $1.15 cada una es 200 por 1.15, que son $230.
hintsEs: ¿Qué operación une un costo por pizza y una cantidad?
Multiplica la tasa por el número de pizzas.

extending.stem: Which relationship is NOT a case of one quantity depending on the other?
choices: A student's height and their house number
extending.explanation: A house number is assigned by an address, not by how tall someone is — the two are unrelated.
choiceFeedback: More study time generally moves the score, so these are related.
These are related — the deck's own example.
These are related — more pizzas use more cheese.
hints: Which pair has no cause between them?
Would growing taller change your address?
Unrelated quantities have no dependence.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál relación NO es un caso de una cantidad que depende de la otra?
extending.explanationEs: El número de una casa lo asigna una dirección, no la estatura de alguien — los dos no están relacionados.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál par no tiene una causa entre ellos?
¿Crecer de estatura cambiaría tu dirección?
Las cantidades no relacionadas no tienen dependencia.

extending.stem: Write the relationship as a sentence: a printer prints 12 pages per minute.
choices: Pages printed depends on minutes running
Minutes running depends on pages printed
12 depends on the number of pages
The printer depends on the pages
extending.explanation: You choose how long to let it run; the number of pages is the result of that choice.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
12 is a fixed rate, not a variable.
The machine itself is not a quantity.
hints: Which is the choice — time or pages?
You start and stop the printer.
Pages come out as a result.
extending.stemEs: Escribe la relación como una oración: una impresora imprime 12 páginas por minuto.
extending.explanationEs: Tú escoges cuánto tiempo dejarla funcionar; el número de páginas es el resultado de esa decisión.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es lo que se escoge — el tiempo o las páginas?
Tú enciendes y apagas la impresora.
Las páginas salen como resultado.

practice.commonMistake: Naming the variables backward — calling the responding quantity 'independent' because it is the one the question asks about.

questions.stem: A ticket costs $8. Which equation represents "8 tickets cost $56"?
questions.explanation: Each of the 8 tickets costs t, so 8 × t = 56. The total is built by multiplying, not by adding.
questions.stemEs: Un boleto cuesta $8. ¿Qué ecuación representa «8 boletos cuestan $56»?
questions.explanationEs: Cada uno de los 8 boletos cuesta t, así que 8 × t = 56. El total se forma multiplicando, no sumando.

questions.explanationEs: x está multiplicada por 4, así que divide los dos lados entre 4: 32 ÷ 4 = 8.

questions.stem: Maya needs at least 20 points to win a prize. Which inequality shows this?
questions.explanation: "At least 20" includes 20 itself, so the symbol must allow equal to: p ≥ 20.
questions.stemEs: Maya necesita al menos 20 puntos para ganar un premio. ¿Qué desigualdad muestra esto?
questions.explanationEs: «Al menos 20» incluye el 20 mismo, así que el símbolo debe permitir igual a: p ≥ 20.

The quantity that changes in response to the independent variable

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Selling Pizzas
revealWordProblem.text:
At a local pizza shop, a customer can order a large pizza with up to three different toppings for $12.49. The shop is open daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and has a total of 6 employees. The shop spends $1.15 on cheese and $1.95 on sauce for each pizza.
Question: How would you describe the relationship between the number of large pizzas sold and each of the following: the hours the shop is open, the number of employees who work in the shop, the cost of cheese each week, and the cost of sauce each week?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A pizzeria sign showing hours of 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and a large pizza with up to 3 toppings for $12.49.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Sort each pair by whether one quantity depends on the other. The hours the shop is open do not change when more pizzas sell — the shop is open 11 to 9 either way — so the hours are independent of pizza sales. The number of employees is also independent day to day; 6 people work whether the shop sells 40 pizzas or 90. Cheese cost does depend on pizzas sold: every pizza uses $1.15 of cheese, so weekly cheese cost = 1.15p, where p is the number of pizzas. Sauce works the same way at $1.95 a pizza, so weekly sauce cost = 1.95p. In both of those, p is the independent variable and the cost is the dependent variable, and each cost grows at a steady rate as p grows.
